answer: Triangulate where agents really run: each epoch, a dozen random peers in different regions send each identity a timed ping, and the round-trip pulse from every vantage point forms a latency fingerprint. Accounts whose fingerprints match too closely are treated as one machine and share a single reward. Each probe is a whisper only its sender can verify, so it can't be replayed. To fake a thousand identities, an attacker must rent real servers in scattered cities and bridge none of them, paying full hosting for every fake.
